# Disambiguate First, Parse Later: Generating Interpretations for Ambiguity Resolution in Semantic Parsing

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#disambiguate-first)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.863.pdf) · Findings of ACL 2025, pp. 16825-16839

**Reading coverage:** All substantive Sections 1-8 and Appendices A-G, Tables 1-9, prompts, training details, examples and figure captions. Reference-list text is not treated as evidence for cited papers.

## Research question

LLMs repeatedly choose preferred readings and omit alternative meanings of ambiguous database questions.

## Method

Prompts an initial interpretation set, trains a LoRA infilling model on missing readings, then parses each reading with a separate SQL model. Training targets use execution-based matching between generated interpretations and annotated SQL; infilling adds interpretations without removing incorrect initial ones.

## Evaluation

AmbiQT with empty-result cases filtered out, AMBROSIA transfer, and a separately re-split AMBROSIA training experiment. Reports single/full reference-interpretation coverage, precision and recall; ablates interpretation generators and parser strength.

## What the results support

Infilling improves coverage over initial prompting and transfers better than the tested in-domain end-to-end fine-tuning baseline. Full AMBROSIA coverage remains 18.8%, with 24.2% precision; end-to-end fine-tuning achieves higher full coverage in several in-domain settings.

## Limits and qualifications

Coverage is relative to annotated readings and database execution, not all possible meanings. Unambiguous evaluation does not penalize extra queries. Parser errors and unfiltered interpretations propagate; single-run training and dataset conventions limit generalization claims.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A modular interpretation-coverage baseline for clarification systems, but generating alternatives does not select actual user intent or prove faithful disambiguation.
